Synopsis:
Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries (Perm, Nizhny Novgorod, Yaroslavl) have driven Russian gasoline output down to ~70% of domestic demand by late August (~80,000 t/day vs. ~115,000 t/day needed). Russia has responded with import measures (Belarus + Asian seaborne, ~7,000 t/day combined), a gasoline export ban through Jan 31, and regional rationing. Even with imports, supply covers only ~85% of demand. The crisis, which began in May, is now in a second acute wave with no near-term resolution visible.
